chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Rib'i ibn 'Abdillah, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding the words of God, Majestic and Mighty: 'They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God' [9:31]

so he said: 'By God! They (the people) neither fasted for them (the religious leaders) nor prayed to them. But rather they (the leaders) permitted for them what was forbidden, and they forbade to them what was permissible — so they (the people) followed them.'

key_terms.أَحْبَار: Rabbis or Jewish scholars; learned religious authorities among the People of the Book
key_terms.أَرْبَاب: Lords, masters, or divine authorities; taking humans as lords means submitting to their religious rulings as if they were divine
key_terms.حَرَام: That which God has declared forbidden
key_terms.حَلَال: That which God has declared permissible
key_terms.رُهْبَان: Christian monks or priests; ascetic religious figures
key_terms.مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ: Besides God; excluding God; in place of God — signifying a rival authority

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it says Jews and Christians took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explains Quran 9:31, which accuses the People of the Book of taking their religious leaders as lords alongside God. The Imam clarifies that this 'lordship' did not mean literal divine worship, but rather blind obedience in matters of religious law — accepting what the priests permitted and forbidden what they prohibited, overriding God's own rulings. This teaching contextualizes the concept of religious authority for early Shia Muslims who lived under the risk of similarly following human authorities over divine law, and it establishes that taqlid (emulation) must ultimately trace back to divinely-authorized sources.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the Words of Allahazwj Majestic and Mighty [9:31] They are taking their Rabbis and their Monks for lords besides Allah.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! They (people) neither Fasted for them (priests) nor prayed to them. But they (priests) permitted for them the Prohibitions, and they prohibited to them the Permissible. Thus they (people) worshipped them (priests)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammed ibn ‘Isa from Rib‘i ibn ‘Abdallah from abu Basir from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“They (unconditionally) obeyed the rabbis and the monks and worshipped the Messiah, son of Mary, as they should have obeyed God . [9:31].’

“By Allah, they (the people) did not pray or fast for them (rabbis and monks) but they (rabbis and monks) made lawful for the people what was unlawful and unlawful what was lawful and people followed them accordingly.”
